limitations_and_boundaries: The analysis of activation functions beyond ReLU and Leaky-ReLU is limited; for non-regular graphs, the proof does not guarantee E(σ(X)) ≤ E(X) for Sigmoid or Tanh.
The experimental study only considers increasing edge weights to a very high value (10000) and does not explore moderate weight increases.
The theoretical bounds rely on the condition s λ̄ < 1 for exponential decay, which may not hold for all weight matrix choices.
The analysis assumes the GCN architecture with augmented normalized Laplacian and does not cover other GNN variants like GAT or GraphSAGE.

research_questions.statement: How does the over-smoothing effect in general graph neural network architectures depend on the weight matrix and the spectrum of the augmented normalized Laplacian?

methods.name: Dirichlet energy tracking
methods.protocol_description: Define Dirichlet energy E(X) = tr(X^T Δ̃ X) for node embeddings X. Prove that each GCN layer component (graph convolution P, weight matrix W, activation σ) reduces Dirichlet energy under certain conditions. Combine lemmas to show exponential decay when s λ̄ < 1, where s is the supremum of the product of squared maximum singular values of weight matrices and λ̄ = (1-λ)^2 with λ the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of Δ̃.

methods.name: Edge perturbation and Dirichlet energy measurement
methods.protocol_description: For each graph, randomly drop or increase weights (to 10000) of a percentage of edges (10%-90%). Compute eigenvalues of normalized Laplacian before and after. Generate signals x as a mix of the first T eigenvectors (T=20 for synthetic, 400 for Cora, 600 for Citeseer) with uniform random coefficients. Compute Dirichlet energy of x, Px, P^2x.
